description.en: Explore four everyday coping comparisons with 24 original paired questions. See raw counts, keep ties and read four complete guides free, without an age estimate.

introduction.en: Compare four groups of current everyday choices: trying or assessing, expressing or processing privately, adapting or keeping structure, and present needs or future plans. Every approach can fit a situation; this is an original preview, without an age or ability verdict.
introduction.zh: 分别回看四组当前日常选择：尝试或评估、表达或独处整理、调整或结构推进、当下需要或未来安排。每种方式都可能符合某些情境；原创预览不判断年龄或能力。

instructions.en: For each scene, choose the approach closer to your more natural response at present. Both are reasonable and there is no correct answer. If neither fits, you can leave and read the guides; all 24 valid choices are needed for a personal record.
instructions.zh: 每个情境选择当前更自然的一种做法，两种都合理，没有正确答案。如果两项都不合适，可以退出直接读指南；个人记录需要24次有效选择。

headline.en: Compare ways of beginning a task

summary.en: A full guide to six original choices about trials and assessment, with concrete scenes, raw counts, ties and optional review.
summary.zh: 完整解释六个原创情境中的尝试与评估，包含具体例子、次数、并列读法和可选回看。

paragraphs.en: These six situations compare beginning with a small trial and first assessing conditions. They concern a new low-risk work tool, an unfamiliar invitation, a canceled plan, learning a skill, an incomplete task brief and a team idea. Each question pairs two reasonable approaches in the same situation. Your choice records which is more natural now; it does not observe how you actually performed the task.
paragraphs.zh: 六个情境比较先做小范围尝试与先评估条件，涉及低风险新工具、陌生活动邀请、计划取消、学习技能、任务要求不完整和团队新想法。同一题的两种做法都可以合理。选择记录当前哪一种更自然，不是对实际任务表现的观察。

paragraphs.en: This is one of four separate comparisons in FermatMind’s original twenty-four-choice preview. The other parts concern organizing feelings, adapting a plan and attending to present or future needs. A choice in this part does not supply an answer to those questions. None of the four parts calculates an inner age, maturity level, cognitive ability or a combined personality type.
paragraphs.zh: 这是费马原创二十四次选择预览中的四组比较之一。其余部分涉及整理感受、调整安排，以及关注当下或未来。这里的选择不能代替其他组的回答。四组都不换算内心年龄、成熟程度、认知能力或综合人格类型。

title.zh: 先做一次有边界的尝试

paragraphs.en: The trial-first side includes trying a small example, joining a short part of an activity, examining options on site, doing a practice exercise, making a changeable draft and suggesting a small experiment. These options describe a way to obtain information through doing. Selecting them more often does not establish curiosity, creativity, speed of learning or a general willingness to take risks.
paragraphs.zh: 先尝试的一侧包括小样例、先参加一小段、看看现场选项、做一个练习、搭可修改雏形和建议小规模试验。这些做法描述通过行动获得信息的顺序。较常选择它们，不确立好奇心、创造力、学习速度或一般冒险倾向。

paragraphs.en: Imagine trying a new note-organizing tool with a few fictional notes after checking that the trial is permitted and safe. The small example may reveal a question you did not know to ask. It might also consume time without answering the important question. Review the scope, effort and information obtained instead of treating the attempt as proof of initiative or a promise that experimentation works better.
paragraphs.zh: 假设先确认许可与安全，再用几条虚构笔记试一个新的整理工具。小样例也许让人发现之前不知道该问的问题，也可能花了时间却没回答关键疑问。应回看尝试范围、投入和获得的信息，不把一次尝试当作行动力证明，或认定试验总是更好。

paragraphs.en: The assessment-first side includes reading instructions, learning the arrangements, checking resources, comparing learning routes, listing unanswered requirements and identifying possible effects. These choices describe an information-gathering order. Selecting them more often does not establish sounder judgment, greater responsibility or more experience, and it does not make the person older or more mature.
paragraphs.zh: 先评估的一侧包括看说明、了解活动安排、确认资源、比较学习路径、列出尚未回答的要求，以及辨认可能影响。这些选择描述先收集信息的顺序。较常选择它们，不确立判断更好、更负责或经验更丰富，也不说明更年长或成熟。

paragraphs.en: For the same fictional tool, a person could first check what it accepts and whether a short trial would answer the task’s needs. That may avoid an unnecessary step, but reading for longer can also postpone useful experience. The questionnaire cannot decide when enough information has been gathered. Check what was learned and whether a decision followed, rather than calling caution either a strength or a fault.
paragraphs.zh: 仍用同一个虚构工具的例子，一个人可以先了解它处理什么，以及短试能否回答任务需要。这样也许避免一次不必要操作，但看资料太久也可能推迟有用体验。问卷不能决定收集多少才算足够。应核对了解了什么、之后是否作出决定，不把谨慎一概定为优点或缺点。

title.en: Read counts without an age conversion

paragraphs.en: A record of four trial-first choices and two assessment-first choices means exactly four and two of these six comparisons. A 5:1 or 6:0 record is a different count of selections, not a stronger personality, a population percentile or an age difference. The question wording and offered alternatives matter: the questionnaire does not count every way that you might respond outside these options.
paragraphs.zh: 先尝试四次、先评估两次，表示这六次比较中分别选择了四次和两次。5:1或6:0是选择次数不同，不是人格更强、人群百分位或年龄差。题目措辞和提供的选项会影响记录；问卷没有统计选项之外的全部可能反应。

paragraphs.en: At 3:3, both sides remain tied. This does not mean perfect balance, an intermediate psychological age or a failed test. The original form requires all twenty-four choices before interpreting any part, even if these six are complete. Missing answers are not estimated. You can leave without a result, and an unfinished form says nothing about memory, maturity or ability.
paragraphs.zh: 3:3时保留两端并列，不表示完美平衡、心理年龄居中或测试失败。原创规则要求二十四次选择都有效，才解释任何一组，即使这一组六题已经完成也一样。缺答不补推断，可以不产生结果直接离开；未完成不说明记忆、成熟程度或能力。

title.en: Two approaches can belong to the same person
title.zh: 同一个人可以使用两种方式

paragraphs.en: In ordinary life, a short trial and a careful review can occur in sequence. You might read enough to set a safe boundary, test a small example and then reassess. The paired format asks you to choose between two first moves in a particular scene. It has not established that trying and assessing are mutually exclusive psychological traits or opposites in every situation.
paragraphs.zh: 现实中，短试与仔细评估可以先后发生。可以先读到足以确认安全边界，再试一个小样例，然后重新评估。二选一只是要求在某个具体情境中比较两种先行做法，没有证明尝试与评估是相互排斥的心理特质，或在所有情境都相反。

paragraphs.en: The less selected side is not missing. Fewer trial choices do not show a lack of initiative, and fewer assessment choices do not show carelessness. Nor does the leading side tell you whether you should choose it on the next task. Use the record to identify a question about a real situation, not to impose a fixed identity on yourself or someone else.
paragraphs.zh: 选择较少的一侧并不缺失。尝试选得少，不说明没有行动力；评估选得少，也不说明粗心。领先一侧同样不能决定下一项任务应该怎样做。记录可以帮助提出一个具体情境问题，不宜据此给自己或他人固定身份。

title.zh: 看看当时具备哪些条件

paragraphs.en: The risk, resources, deadline and clarity of a task can change which first move seems practical. Access also matters: a person may lack permission, time or materials for a trial, or may need to act before more information becomes available. These are possible contextual explanations, not conclusions inferred from your answers. A count does not separate preference from opportunity.
paragraphs.zh: 任务风险、资源、期限和要求是否清晰，都可能改变哪种先行做法更可行。机会也重要：可能没有试用许可、时间或材料，也可能需要在资料齐全前行动。这些只是需要核对的情境解释，不是由回答推断的结论。次数无法区分偏好与机会。

paragraphs.en: A different response on a later visit could reflect a new task or current state. It would not by itself prove that you became more confident, cautious, younger or older. Likewise, this comparison cannot explain the other three parts or rank them as better ways of coping. Each part records a different set of forced choices and leaves many details unmeasured.
paragraphs.zh: 后来重新选择不同，也许涉及新任务或当下状态，本身不能证明更自信、更谨慎、更年轻或更年长。这组也不能解释另外三组，更不能给应对方式排好坏。每组记录的是不同的一组强制相对选择，还有许多细节没有测量。

title.en: One optional review of a real task

paragraphs.en: If you want to explore the comparison, choose one ordinary, low-risk task. Privately note the first move, the constraints checked, the information obtained and whether the plan changed. You could try one bounded example or check one important requirement; neither action is required by a result. Do not use an exercise to bypass real safety, consent or work rules.
paragraphs.zh: 如果愿意探索，可以选择一项普通、低风险任务，私下记录先做了什么、核对哪些限制、获得什么信息，以及是否调整安排。可以做一个有边界的小样例，也可以先核对一条关键要求；结果不要求采取任何一种行动。不要为练习绕过现实安全、同意或工作规则。

paragraphs.en: A useful review can end with keeping the current approach, combining both approaches or deciding that more information is needed. An unclear outcome is acceptable. The exercise does not test willpower and promises no improvement. The facts worth checking are what happened and what was workable for that task, rather than whether the outcome confirms a label.
paragraphs.zh: 回看可以以保留现有做法、结合两种顺序或认为还需信息结束。结论不清楚也可以。这不是意志力考验，不承诺改善。值得核对的是实际发生什么、对这项任务是否可行，而不是结果有没有印证某个标签。

paragraphs.en: These six comparisons belong to FermatMind’s original coping-rhythm form. They are not the COPE, Brief COPE, CRI or a psychological-age scale, and evidence for those different measures does not validate this item set. The construct and scoring have not completed psychometric validation; the English wording is a working translation. No reliability, accuracy, norms or age-equivalence figures are supplied.
paragraphs.zh: 这六次比较属于费马原创应对节奏题本，不是COPE、Brief COPE、CRI或心理年龄量表；不同量表的证据不能验证这组题目。构念与计分尚未完成心理测量学验证，英文是工作译文，不提供信度、准确率、常模或年龄换算数据。

paragraphs.en: The record cannot decide medical or legal questions, hiring or promotion, education admission, security permissions, financial decisions or suitability for a relationship. It does not assess intelligence, attention, memory, cognitive decline or mental health. A public guide contains no one’s responses and can be read without taking the form. Treat its scenes as examples, not as an account of a particular reader.
paragraphs.zh: 记录不能用于医疗或司法判断、录用晋升、升学录取、安全权限、金融决策或关系筛选，也不评价智力、注意力、记忆、认知衰退或心理健康。公开指南不含任何人的回答，无需作答也可以阅读。场景是假设例子，不是在描述某个读者。

scoreReading.en: Each side records 0–6 choices within this six-comparison group. A 3:3 tie keeps both; four separate groups form no overall score, age or combined type.
scoreReading.zh: 两侧分别记录本组六次比较中0—6次选择；3:3保留并列。四组分开，不合总分、年龄或综合类型。

title.en: Trying First and Assessing First: A Full Free Guide
title.zh: 先尝试与先评估：六个情境的完整读法

description.en: Read six choices about trials and assessment, compare concrete examples, understand raw counts and ties, and try one optional review without an age label.
description.zh: 阅读六个关于小范围尝试与谨慎评估的选择，理解具体例子、原始次数和并列，以及一次可选回看，不换算年龄。

summary.en: Read six paired scenes about speaking and private reflection, with concrete examples, counts, ties and privacy-aware observations.
summary.zh: 完整阅读六组表达与独处情境，通过具体例子、次数、并列和隐私条件理解整理方式。

title.en: Two ways of sorting out a feeling

paragraphs.en: These six choices concern an uncomfortable meeting, a decision with mixed feelings, good news, a conflict that has ended, accumulating stress and a disappointment. They compare putting an experience into words with first making room to process it privately. The topic is the order and setting of reflection, rather than whether feelings are present or how intense they are.
paragraphs.zh: 六个情境涉及让人不舒服的会议、感受复杂的决定、好消息、已结束的冲突、逐渐累积的压力和期待落空。比较的是把体验说出来，与先留一点私下整理空间。关注反思的顺序和场合，不是有没有感受或感受有多强。

paragraphs.en: One side includes talking to someone trusted, describing what happened and finding the main point through words. The other includes quiet thought, writing, walking alone or first taking in an experience before choosing when to share. A response records the approach that feels more natural in the question; it does not show whether an actual conversation or private reflection helped.
paragraphs.zh: 一侧包括向可信的人说说、复述经过和通过语言找重点；另一侧包括安静思考、书写、独自散步，或先自己体会，再选择何时分享。回答记录题目里哪种做法更自然，不说明现实中的交流或独处有没有帮助。

title.zh: 表达可以让哪些细节显现

paragraphs.en: Imagine leaving a difficult meeting and telling a trusted colleague which moment felt uncomfortable. While recounting it, you may notice that an unclear expectation matters more than the meeting’s overall tone. Or you may still be unsure afterward. The useful questions are what became clearer and how the other person responded, rather than whether speaking counts as the correct way to process a feeling.
paragraphs.zh: 假设一次会议让人不舒服，之后向可信同事讲起某个时刻。复述时，也许发现最在意的是期待不清楚，而不是整场会议的气氛；说完也可能仍不确定。值得问的是哪些细节更清楚了、对方怎样回应，而不是开口是不是正确的整理方式。

paragraphs.en: Talking requires a workable context: someone available, enough trust and room to choose what to disclose. An unhelpful response can make the conversation less useful without proving that expression was a mistake. A higher count for this side does not establish emotional intelligence, confidence, social skill or healthier feelings. Expression is not a promise of relief or a requirement to tell someone everything.
paragraphs.zh: 交流需要可行条件：对方有空、关系可信，也有空间决定透露多少。回应不合适，可能使交流不那么有用，却不证明表达本身做错了。选得较多不确立情商、自信、社交能力或情绪更健康；表达不保证轻松，也不要求把一切告诉别人。

title.en: What private processing can make room for
title.zh: 私下整理可以保留哪些空间

paragraphs.en: For the same meeting, another person might first write a few private sentences or walk quietly before deciding whether to discuss it. The pause can separate the sequence of events from an immediate reaction. It can also leave an important message unsent for longer than intended. Review the later decision and whether communication was needed, rather than assuming that time alone either solves or worsens the situation.
paragraphs.zh: 还是同一次会议，另一个人可能先私下写几句或安静走一会儿，再决定要不要谈。暂停也许帮助区分经过与即时反应，也可能让一条重要信息比原打算更晚发出。应回看之后的决定和是否需要沟通，不预设独处必然解决或加重情况。

paragraphs.en: Private processing is not automatically suppression, withdrawal or avoidance, and it does not create an obligation to disclose later. Practical conditions matter: a quiet space may be available or absent, and privacy may be especially important in one relationship. A higher count cannot establish deeper reflection, greater maturity or a mental-health concern; a lower count does not mean that you lack an inner life.
paragraphs.zh: 私下整理不自动等于压抑、退缩或回避，也不会产生之后必须公开表达的义务。现实条件同样重要：可能有或没有安静空间，某段关系中的隐私可能尤其需要保护。次数较多不确立反思更深、更成熟或存在心理健康困扰；次数较少也不说明缺少内在体验。

title.en: What four, two and a tie mean
title.zh: 四次、两次与并列意味着什么

paragraphs.en: Four expression choices and two private-processing choices are a 4:2 record for this particular group. A 5:1 or 6:0 record contains a different balance of offered choices; it is not a score for emotional competence or the amount of support needed. Someone may talk first in one of the six scenes and prefer privacy in another. The overall count does not identify which scene mattered most.
paragraphs.zh: 表达四次、私下整理两次，是本组六题的4:2记录。5:1或6:0表示所给选项的次数组合不同，不是情绪能力分数，也不决定需要多少支持。一个人可能在六种情境之一先说出来，在另一种里更愿意独处；总次数不能指出哪个场景最重要。

paragraphs.en: At 3:3, keep both approaches without choosing a winner. The tie does not establish perfect emotional balance or an intermediate personality. All twenty-four questions must have valid choices before any group is interpreted. An incomplete form produces no substitute result, and missing answers should not be read as difficulty understanding feelings, poor memory or a reluctance to cooperate.
paragraphs.zh: 3:3时保留两种做法，不指定赢家，不据此认定情绪完美平衡或人格居中。二十四题都需要有效选择，才解释任何一组。未完成时不生成替代结果，也不把缺答读成难以理解情绪、记忆不好或不愿配合。

title.en: Both can happen in one sequence
title.zh: 两种做法可以先后发生

paragraphs.en: You could first sort out a feeling privately and then explain one part of it, or talk first and later reflect alone. Such a sequence is compatible with either side being selected more often in the questionnaire. The paired format has not demonstrated that the two approaches are mutually exclusive traits. It records a relative first choice under the wording of six scenes.
paragraphs.zh: 可以先私下理清感受，再解释其中一部分；也可以先谈，再独自回看。无论问卷哪侧选得多，都可能出现这种顺序。二选一没有证明它们是相互排斥的特质，只记录六个场景措辞下的相对先行选择。

paragraphs.en: The less selected approach is still available. Fewer speaking choices do not prove introversion or weak communication, while fewer private choices do not prove a lack of reflection. This part also cannot determine the other three comparisons about trying, structuring a plan or attending to future needs. Keep the groups separate rather than assembling a label that claims to explain the whole person.
paragraphs.zh: 选择较少的做法仍然可以使用。说得少不证明内向或沟通弱，独处选得少也不证明缺乏反思。这组不能决定另外三组关于尝试、安排结构或未来需要的比较；应分开阅读，不拼成解释整个人的标签。

title.zh: 隐私、信任与可获得支持

paragraphs.en: A trusted person being unavailable can affect a choice, as can having no quiet space. The emotional topic, relationship and need for privacy can change what seems workable. These are details to check in a real example, not causes established by a test result. The questionnaire cannot separate an enduring preference from the options that happened to be available.
paragraphs.zh: 可信的人暂时不在，或没有安静空间，都可能影响选择。话题、关系和隐私需要也会改变哪种做法可行。这些应在具体事例中核对，不是测试确立的原因。问卷无法区分持续偏好与当时恰好具备的选项。

paragraphs.en: A different answer later does not, by itself, show better emotional health or a move toward maturity. Nor can the count decide whether a private or professional conversation is needed. A concern that matters outside the questionnaire deserves to be considered in its actual circumstances; the record supplies neither a clinical assessment nor a threshold for seeking appropriate support.
paragraphs.zh: 后来回答不同，本身不表示情绪更健康或走向成熟。次数也不能决定是否需要一次私人或专业交流。现实中重要的困扰，应按实际情境看待；记录既不提供临床评估，也不划定寻求合适支持的门槛。

paragraphs.en: Choose one ordinary, low-risk event if you want to look more closely. Privately note how you began processing it and what became clearer afterward. You might say a short piece to someone trusted or write a few sentences only for yourself. Either way, choose a setting that respects your privacy and the other person’s willingness to listen.
paragraphs.zh: 如果愿意，可以选一件普通、低风险事件，私下记下自己先怎样整理，之后什么更清楚了。可以只向可信的人说一小段，也可以只为自己写几句；都应选择尊重自身隐私、对方也愿意倾听的场合。

paragraphs.en: There is no need to repeat the exercise, upload a note or prove that one method works. You can keep the current approach, combine both or stop. A useful observation may simply identify what kind of time, space or conversation would be more workable next time. It does not need to produce a personality conclusion or a story about your age.
paragraphs.zh: 无需重复练习、上传笔记或证明哪种方法有效。可以保留现有方式、结合两种，或直接停止。有用的观察也许只是看出下次怎样的时间、空间或交流更可行，不必得到人格结论，也不必编成关于年龄的故事。

paragraphs.en: This guide explains one part of FermatMind’s original coping-rhythm preview. It is not the COPE, Brief COPE, CRI, an emotional-intelligence test or a psychological-age measure. Research on different instruments does not validate these six paired questions. The construct and scoring have not completed psychometric validation, and the English text is a working translation.
paragraphs.zh: 本指南解释费马原创应对节奏预览的一部分，不是COPE、Brief COPE、CRI、情商测试或心理年龄测量。其他工具的研究不能验证这六道配对题；构念和计分尚未完成心理测量学验证，英文是工作译文。

paragraphs.en: Do not use the record for diagnosis, cognitive or mental-health judgments, hiring, promotion, admissions, legal or financial decisions, security permissions or relationship screening. It contains no age estimate, maturity grade or prediction of another person’s response. Public explanations can be read independently of answering and contain no one’s private attempt.
paragraphs.zh: 记录不能用于诊断、认知或心理健康判断、招聘晋升、录取、法律金融决策、安全权限或关系筛选，没有年龄估计、成熟等级或他人反应预测。公开解释可以独立阅读，不含任何人的私人答卷。

scoreReading.en: Each side records 0–6 choices within this six-comparison group. A 3:3 tie keeps both; four separate groups form no overall score, age or combined type.
scoreReading.zh: 两侧分别记录本组六次比较中0—6次选择；3:3保留并列。四组分开，不合总分、年龄或综合类型。

title.en: Expression and Private Processing: A Full Free Guide
title.zh: 表达整理与私下梳理：六个情境的完整读法

description.en: Explore speaking and private reflection through six paired scenes, counts, ties and concrete examples, without an emotional-skill or psychological-age verdict.
description.zh: 通过六个配对情境、次数、并列和具体例子理解表达与独处，不据此判断情绪能力、成熟程度或心理年龄。

summary.en: Explore six choices about changed plans, priorities and routines, with concrete examples, raw counts, ties and a practical review.
summary.zh: 通过具体例子、原始次数、并列读法和一次回看，理解六个关于计划变化、优先顺序与例行的选择。

title.en: What changes when a plan meets reality

paragraphs.en: These six scenes concern an interrupted day, an obstacle in a long task, changed travel arrangements, a new collaboration, a change in energy and several tasks arriving together. They compare adjusting the route to current conditions with using a checklist, milestones or a minimum routine to keep moving. Both options can be reasonable; the question asks which is more natural now.
paragraphs.zh: 六个场景涉及一天被打断、长期任务受阻、出行变化、新合作、精力变化和多件事同时出现。比较按现场条件调整路径，与借助清单、节点或最低限度例行继续推进。两种做法都可以合理，问题只是当前哪种更自然。

paragraphs.en: The record does not observe whether a project finished or an arrangement worked. It counts choices offered in six particular situations. A person can change the order while keeping a milestone, or retain a routine while changing the method. Read this group as a comparison of approaches rather than a test of reliability, adaptability or project-management skill.
paragraphs.zh: 记录没有观察项目是否完成、安排是否有效，只统计六个具体情境中所给选项的选择。可以换顺序而保留节点，也可以保留例行而改变方法。应把它读成做法比较，不是可靠性、应变或项目管理能力测试。

paragraphs.en: The adjusting side includes reordering priorities, trying another method, responding to conditions on site, revising a division of work as it develops, choosing a task that fits current energy and switching order with progress. These are different actions sharing a focus on the situation. More selections do not establish quick thinking or success in unfamiliar environments.
paragraphs.zh: 调整的一侧包括重排优先顺序、换方法、回应现场情况、边做边改分工、选择符合当前精力的任务，以及按进展换序。这些是不同动作，共同点是关注情境。选得较多，不确立思维更快或一定能适应陌生环境。

paragraphs.en: Imagine a small team task whose required material arrives late. You could move a ready part forward and return to the delayed part later. That might make the day more workable, but frequent changes could also cause an important checkpoint to be missed. Review which change was made, who needed to know and what still got finished; do not use the choice count as proof that flexibility helped.
paragraphs.zh: 假设小组任务所需材料晚到，可以先推进已经具备条件的部分，之后再回来。这也许让当天更可行，但频繁变化也可能遗漏重要检查点。应回看改了什么、谁需要知道、哪些仍然完成，不用选择次数证明灵活一定有帮助。

title.en: Keeping a route that can be checked
title.zh: 保留一条可核对的推进路径

paragraphs.en: The structured side includes rebuilding a checklist, keeping milestones and a regular pace, confirming a revised route before acting, clarifying roles, retaining a minimum routine and finishing one scheduled work block first. These options offer a way to check progress. More selections do not establish discipline, competence or a greater sense of responsibility.
paragraphs.zh: 结构的一侧包括重建清单、保留节点和固定节奏、行动前确认新路线、明确角色、保留最低限度例行，以及先完成一个已排定工作块。它们提供核对进展的方式。选得较多，不确立更自律、更有能力或责任感更强。

paragraphs.en: For the same delayed task, another person might revise the checklist and tell the team which checkpoint remains. This can make the next step explicit, while a very detailed structure can also become burdensome or leave little room for changing conditions. Check whether the list helped the actual work. A written plan and a completed outcome are different facts.
paragraphs.zh: 还是材料晚到的任务，另一个人可能先改清单，说明哪个检查点仍要保留。这样可以让下一步明确，但结构过密也可能成为负担，或留不下应对变化的空间。应核对清单有没有帮助实际工作；写出计划与完成结果是不同事实。

title.en: Read six selections as six selections
title.zh: 六次选择就是六次选择

paragraphs.en: A 4:2 record means one approach was chosen in four of the six scenes and the other in two. A 5:1 or 6:0 count does not establish a greater amount of a trait or predict better performance. The same count can come from different scenes, and the questions do not measure how often you use either approach in an ordinary week.
paragraphs.zh: 4:2表示一种做法在六个场景里选了四次，另一种选了两次。5:1或6:0不确立某种特质更多，也不预测表现更好。同样次数可能来自不同场景，题目没有测量普通一周里两种方式分别使用多少次。

paragraphs.en: A 3:3 tie retains both sides without turning them into a superior balanced style. All twenty-four choices must be valid before any of the four groups is interpreted. Missing answers are not filled from earlier choices or another group. You can stop without a result; an unfinished form gives no basis for judging planning ability or willingness to follow through.
paragraphs.zh: 3:3并列保留两侧，不把它变成更优越的平衡风格。二十四次选择都有效，才解释四组中的任何一组。缺答不根据前面的回答或别组来填补。可以不产生结果直接停止，未完成不提供判断计划能力或执行意愿的依据。

title.en: Adjust the method while keeping an anchor
title.zh: 调整方法，也可以保留支点

paragraphs.en: An ordinary plan may use both approaches: preserve an essential deadline while changing the order of optional work, or keep a small daily routine while revising its size. The forced choice does not demonstrate that flexibility and structure are incompatible. It asks you to compare two described first responses, leaving many combined approaches outside the options.
paragraphs.zh: 普通安排可以同时用两种方式：保留关键期限，调整可选工作顺序；或保留一个日常例行，改变它的大小。二选一没有证明灵活与结构不相容，只让人比较两种被描述的先行反应，许多组合方式不在选项中。

paragraphs.en: The less selected side is not a defect. Fewer flexible choices do not establish rigidity, and fewer structured choices do not establish irresponsibility. Neither result determines whether a particular task needs a fixed process. That depends on its real requirements and role obligations, which a general questionnaire cannot replace.
paragraphs.zh: 选择较少的一侧不是缺点。灵活选得少不确立僵化，结构选得少也不确立不负责。哪种记录都不能决定某项任务是否需要固定流程；这取决于现实要求与职责，一份通用问卷无法替代。

title.en: Resources, roles and energy belong in the reading
title.zh: 把资源、角色与精力放回解释中

paragraphs.en: Available resources, the consequences of a change, role responsibilities and current health or energy can affect which action seems workable. A person may need to keep a checkpoint even when a different order feels easier. These possibilities are prompts for checking context, not explanations inferred from your answers. The count does not distinguish a free preference from a necessary constraint.
paragraphs.zh: 可用资源、改动的影响、角色责任，以及当下健康或精力，都可能影响哪种动作可行。即使换顺序更轻松，也可能需要保留某个检查点。这些是核对情境的线索，不是由回答推断的解释；次数无法区分自由偏好与必要限制。

paragraphs.en: A different record later does not by itself show improved executive ability, greater maturity or a change in psychological age. This group also cannot determine whether someone would be a good employee or collaborator. Review a specific arrangement and what happened afterward rather than using an overall count to judge someone’s potential.
paragraphs.zh: 后来记录不同，本身不说明执行能力改善、更成熟或心理年龄变化。这组也不能决定谁会是好员工或好搭档。应核对某个安排及之后发生了什么，不用总次数评价一个人的潜力。

title.en: One optional review of a changed plan

paragraphs.en: Choose one ordinary, low-risk plan if you want to examine the contrast. Note what changed, which requirement stayed fixed and what you did next. You might revise one priority or rebuild one short checklist. Respect any actual safety or work requirements; a questionnaire record is not permission to ignore them. There is no need to share the note.
paragraphs.zh: 如果愿意，可以选一个普通、低风险安排，记下变了什么、什么要求仍然固定，以及下一步做了什么。可以调整一项优先顺序，也可以重建一张短清单。仍需尊重现实安全或工作要求，问卷记录不是忽略它们的许可，也无需分享笔记。

paragraphs.en: Then ask whether important work remained visible, what got completed and whether the arrangement became burdensome. Keeping the approach, combining both or declining further exercises are all possible outcomes. The review promises no productivity gain and does not require uninterrupted performance. It can simply help make the next practical question more specific.
paragraphs.zh: 再问重要事项是否仍然清楚、完成了什么、安排有没有变成负担。可以保留做法、结合两种，也可以不再练习。回看不承诺提高产出，不要求始终高效；也许只是帮助把下一个现实问题说得更具体。

title.en: What this original comparison cannot assess
title.zh: 这组原创比较不能评估什么

paragraphs.en: These six scenes form part of FermatMind’s original coping-rhythm preview. They are not an established measure of executive function, work performance or psychological age. The four paired constructs have not completed psychometric validation, and the English wording is a working translation. Evidence for other coping questionnaires does not establish validity for this form.
paragraphs.zh: 这六个场景是费马原创应对节奏预览的一部分，不是已确立的执行功能、工作表现或心理年龄测量。四组配对构念尚未完成心理测量学验证，英文是工作译文；其他应对问卷的证据不能确立本题本效度。

paragraphs.en: There is no overall score, maturity grade, combined type or age conversion. Do not use the record for medical or cognitive judgments, hiring or promotion, education admissions, legal or financial decisions, security permissions or relationship screening. Public explanations contain no one’s responses and can be read without answering the questionnaire.
paragraphs.zh: 没有总分、成熟等级、综合类型或年龄换算。记录不能用于医疗认知判断、招聘晋升、升学录取、法律金融决策、安全权限或关系筛选。公开解释不含任何人的回答，无需作答也可阅读。

headline.en: Compare routes through a changed plan
headline.zh: 比较计划变化后的推进路径

scoreReading.en: Each side records 0–6 choices within this six-comparison group. A 3:3 tie keeps both; four separate groups form no overall score, age or combined type.
scoreReading.zh: 两侧分别记录本组六次比较中0—6次选择；3:3保留并列。四组分开，不合总分、年龄或综合类型。

title.en: Adapting Plans and Keeping Structure: A Full Guide
title.zh: 灵活调整与结构推进：六次选择怎样读

description.en: Read six choices about disrupted plans, flexible changes and practical structure, with raw counts, ties and a small review rather than a performance grade.
description.zh: 阅读六个关于计划打断、灵活变化和推进结构的选择，理解原始次数、并列和一次回看，不评价工作表现。

title.en: Meeting Present Needs and Planning Ahead

summary.en: A complete guide to six choices about immediate needs and later commitments, with examples, raw counts, ties and a realistic observation exercise.
summary.zh: 完整解释六个关于眼前需要与未来约定的选择，包含具体例子、原始次数、并列和可选的现实观察。

title.en: Which need receives the first response

paragraphs.en: These six scenes compare first responding to an immediate need with first connecting an action to a longer plan. They concern an unexpectedly free evening, a weekend, a new opportunity, a busy day, a learning choice and a changed plan. Both alternatives can be worthwhile. The question is which described first move is more natural at present, rather than which kind of life is better.
paragraphs.zh: 六个场景比较先回应眼前需要，与先把行动连接到较长期安排，涉及意外空闲的晚上、周末、新机会、忙碌一天、学习选择和计划变化。两种选项都可能值得做，问题是当前哪种先行做法更自然，不是哪一种生活更好。

paragraphs.en: One side includes rest or activity needed today, practical needs that have accumulated, a current experience, an immediate response, a problem now and making today workable again. The other includes later use, next month’s preparation, a long-term direction, protected goal time, reusable foundations and revised future milestones. The record does not show whether any of those actions actually occurred.
paragraphs.zh: 一侧包括当天需要的休息或活动、积累的现实需要、当前体验、即时回应、眼前问题和让今天恢复可行动；另一侧包括之后的用途、下个月准备、长期方向、保护目标时间、可反复使用的基础和未来节点调整。记录没有观察这些动作是否实际发生。

paragraphs.en: Imagine a weekend with one unexpected open hour. A person might first address a small task that has been making the current week harder, or choose needed rest. That can be a practical response to today’s conditions, while a recurring future task might still need a later place. The meaningful details are what needed attention and whether the other commitment remained visible.
paragraphs.zh: 假设周末意外多出一个小时，一个人可能先处理让本周不顺的一件小事，或选择当下需要的休息。这样可以回应当天条件，而某项长期任务仍可能需要另找时间。重要细节是什么需要回应，以及另一个约定是否仍然清楚。

paragraphs.en: Selecting present-focused options more often does not establish short-sightedness, indulgence or a lack of planning. Nor does it prove an ability to live in the moment. Resources, health, responsibilities and available time may make immediate needs especially important. The questionnaire cannot decide how much of a choice comes from preference and how much comes from what is currently possible.
paragraphs.zh: 当下选项较多，不确立短视、享乐或缺少规划，也不证明更会活在当下。资源、健康、责任和可支配时间可能使眼前需要特别重要。问卷不能决定一个选择有多少来自偏好，又有多少来自当前能做到的事。

paragraphs.en: For the same open hour, another person might prepare one small part of next month’s project or practice a foundation likely to be used again. This could keep a later commitment visible, but it might also postpone something important today. Review what was prepared and what immediate need remained; do not assume that an action with a later purpose was automatically more valuable.
paragraphs.zh: 还是这个空闲小时，另一个人可能先准备下个月项目的一小部分，或练习以后可能反复用到的基础。这样也许保留了未来节点，却也可能推迟当天的重要需要。应回看准备了什么、眼前还有什么，不预设只要用途在未来就更有价值。

paragraphs.en: More future-planning selections do not establish maturity, self-discipline, intelligence or a higher chance of success. The person may have more room to prepare, or the later deadline may already be pressing. Less frequent selection of this side does not establish a lack of goals. A choice count cannot predict the future or judge how well a long-term plan will work.
paragraphs.zh: 未来安排选得多，不确立成熟、自律、聪明或更高成功概率；也许只是更有准备空间，或后面的期限已经逼近。较少选择这一侧，不说明没有目标。次数无法预测未来，也不能评价长期计划会不会有效。

title.en: Read the counts within this group

paragraphs.en: Four present-needs choices and two future-plan choices mean four and two selections in these six scenes. A 5:1 or 6:0 record is a different response pattern, not an age, maturity score or population comparison. The offered alternatives shape the count. It does not measure how much time you actually spend on either kind of activity.
paragraphs.zh: 当下需要四次、未来安排两次，表示六个场景里分别选了四次和两次。5:1或6:0是回答组合不同，不是年龄、成熟分数或人群比较。所给选项会影响次数，记录没有测量实际花在两类活动上的时间。

paragraphs.en: At 3:3, both sides remain tied. This does not identify an ideal balance or an age halfway between two extremes. All twenty-four choices must be valid before interpreting any group. Missing answers are not inferred from the other scenes or from another part; leaving without a result does not establish a problem with attention, planning or commitment.
paragraphs.zh: 3:3保留两端并列，不指认理想平衡，也不对应两个极端之间的某个年龄。二十四次选择都有效，才解释任何一组。缺答不从其他场景或部分推断；直接离开而不产生结果，不确立注意、规划或投入意愿的问题。

title.en: A day and a longer plan can support each other
title.zh: 当天安排与长期计划可以并存

paragraphs.en: Handling an immediate need can make a later task possible, and a small advance on a future task can change what tomorrow requires. These are possible sequences to examine in real life, not a causal model established by the form. A person can attend to both within the same day. The forced choice compares two first moves and leaves many combinations unrecorded.
paragraphs.zh: 处理眼前需要，也许让之后的任务成为可能；为未来推进一点，也可能改变明天的需要。这些是在现实中可以核对的顺序，不是表单建立的因果模型。同一天可以兼顾两者，二选一只比较两种先行做法，许多组合没有被记录。

paragraphs.en: The less selected side is not absent. This group also does not determine whether you prefer a trial, private reflection or a checklist in the other parts. Four leading sides should not be assembled into an age profile or personality type. Read a particular scene and ask which need was described, which alternative was missing and what the choice leaves unknown.
paragraphs.zh: 选择较少的一侧并不缺失。这组也不能决定其他部分会选尝试、独处梳理还是清单推进。四组领先侧不应拼成年龄档案或人格类型。应回到某个场景，问它描述了什么需要、少了什么选项，以及一个选择还有什么解释不了。

paragraphs.en: An urgent responsibility, a period of poor health, a change of work stage or limited free time can affect which need comes first. Someone with room to prepare may make a different choice from someone handling an immediate constraint. These are contextual possibilities, not explanations assigned to a reader by the questionnaire. The same person may choose differently when those conditions change.
paragraphs.zh: 紧迫责任、健康不佳的阶段、职业阶段变化或空闲时间有限，都可能影响先回应什么。能够提前准备的人，与正在处理眼前限制的人，可能有不同选择。这些是情境可能性，不是问卷给读者指定的解释；条件改变时，同一个人也可能选得不同。

paragraphs.en: A later change in the record does not by itself establish personal growth, deterioration or a change in cognitive age. Nor does one side’s count decide whether someone is responsible or suitable for a role. A practical discussion needs details about the actual commitments and resources, rather than treating future attention as a moral achievement or present attention as a failure.
paragraphs.zh: 后来记录改变，本身不确立成长、退步或认知年龄变化。某一侧的次数也不能决定一个人是否负责、适合某个角色。现实讨论需要具体约定与资源细节，不把关注未来当作道德成就，也不把关注当下当作失败。

title.en: One optional comparison of two needs

paragraphs.en: If useful, choose one ordinary, low-risk decision and name the immediate need and one later commitment privately. Note what time or resources were available and what you chose to do first. You could make room for one necessary task today or a short period for a later task. Neither is required by the record, and you do not need to upload or share the note.
paragraphs.zh: 如果觉得有用，可以选一个普通、低风险决定，私下说清眼前需要和一个之后的约定，记下有哪些时间或资源、先做了什么。可以给今天一件必要的事留空间，也可以给以后的一项任务留一小段时间。记录不要求选择哪一种，也无需上传或分享笔记。

paragraphs.en: Review what was addressed and what still needs a place, rather than scoring the choice as good or bad. The observation can end with keeping the arrangement, combining approaches, asking for more information or stopping. It promises no improvement in productivity or well-being. Its purpose is to make a concrete next question easier to discuss, without an age or ability verdict.
paragraphs.zh: 回看回应了什么、还有什么需要安排，不给选择打好坏分。可以保留现有安排、结合两种方式、继续了解情况或停止观察，不承诺提高产出或幸福感；只是让一个具体的后续问题更容易讨论，不给年龄或能力判词。

title.en: Original preview, without an age model
title.zh: 原创预览，没有年龄模型

paragraphs.en: This is one part of FermatMind’s original coping-rhythm form. Its everyday-choice focus does not provide a psychological-age conversion. The construct and scoring have not completed psychometric validation, and the English text is a working translation. It is not the COPE, Brief COPE, CRI or a validated measure of planning, self-control or cognitive function.
paragraphs.zh: 这是费马原创应对节奏题本的一部分，围绕日常选择的主题，不提供心理年龄换算。构念与计分尚未完成心理测量学验证，英文是工作译文；它不是COPE、Brief COPE、CRI，也不是经验证的规划、自控或认知功能测量。

paragraphs.en: There is no overall total, combined type, maturity grade or comparison with people of the same age. Do not use the record for medical, legal, financial, employment, admission, security or relationship decisions. It does not evaluate memory, attention, intelligence or mental health. The complete public guide can be read without providing any responses and contains no one’s private record.
paragraphs.zh: 没有总分、综合类型、成熟等级或同龄比较。记录不能用于医疗、法律、金融、就业、录取、安全权限或关系决策，也不评价记忆、注意力、智力或心理健康。完整公开指南无需提供回答即可阅读，不含任何人的私人记录。

headline.en: Read two kinds of priorities in context
headline.zh: 把两类优先需要放回情境

scoreReading.en: Each side records 0–6 choices within this six-comparison group. A 3:3 tie keeps both; four separate groups form no overall score, age or combined type.
scoreReading.zh: 两侧分别记录本组六次比较中0—6次选择；3:3保留并列。四组分开，不合总分、年龄或综合类型。

title.en: Present Needs and Future Plans: A Full Free Guide
title.zh: 当下需要与未来安排：六次选择的完整读法

description.en: Compare immediate needs and longer commitments in six paired scenes. Read counts, ties, realistic examples and an optional observation without an age estimate.
description.zh: 在六个配对情境中比较眼前需要与长期约定，阅读次数、并列、具体例子和可选观察，不估计心理年龄。

paragraphs.en: This form migrates FermatMind’s original twenty-four paired choices from the local Mini program. The Chinese prompts and two options are retained, including their balanced A/B positions. English is a working translation. These four comparisons are not the COPE, Brief COPE, CRI or an established psychological-age measure.
paragraphs.zh: 本页迁移费马小程序完整原创二十四次配对选择，保留中文题目、两项选项及平衡的A／B位置。英文是工作译文。四组比较不是COPE、Brief COPE、CRI或已确立的心理年龄测量。

paragraphs.en: The constructs and scoring have not completed psychometric validation. There are no published reliability, validity, accuracy, norms or age-conversion figures for this form. Research about other coping questionnaires does not establish evidence for these items or their English wording.
paragraphs.zh: 构念和计分尚未完成心理测量学验证，本题本没有已发表的信度、效度、准确率、常模或年龄换算数据。其他应对问卷的研究不能验证这些题目或当前英文译文。

title.zh: 两种合理选项，二十四次选择

paragraphs.en: For each scene, choose which of two equally reasonable approaches is closer to your more natural response at present. There is no birth-date or age field. The form covers ordinary tasks and experiences rather than testing how well you handle them.
paragraphs.zh: 每个情境从两种同样可取的做法里，选择当前更自然的一种。表单不读取出生日期或年龄，讨论普通任务与体验，不测试处理得好不好。

paragraphs.en: The source has no skip option: all twenty-four choices must be valid before any group is interpreted. If neither choice fits, you can leave and read all public guides without a result. Unfinished forms receive no inferred or replacement interpretation, and you need not give an answer just to finish.
paragraphs.zh: 原题本没有跳过选项，二十四次选择都有效，才解释任何一组。如果两项都不合适，可以直接离开、无分阅读所有公开指南。未完成不补推断或替代解释，无需为了结束而硬选。

title.en: Four separate counts, no overall total
title.zh: 四组次数分开，不合总分

paragraphs.en: Each group has six comparisons and two sides; choosing an option adds one to its side. The two counts always sum to six after a complete form. For example, four choices on one side leave two on the other. No group is compared with another group’s count.
paragraphs.zh: 每组六次比较、两侧，选择一项就给该侧加一次；完整作答后两侧合计六次。例如，一侧四次，另一侧就两次。不同组的次数不互相比较。

paragraphs.en: A 4:2, 5:1 or 6:0 record describes the offered choices, not frequency in life, the strength of a trait or a population percentile. A side with more selections is not automatically better, and the less selected side is neither missing nor a defect.
paragraphs.zh: 4:2、5:1或6:0描述所给选项的选择情况，不是现实使用频率、特质强度或人群百分位。选得多不自动更好，选得少的一侧也不缺失或是缺点。

paragraphs.en: When a group is 3:3, retain both sides. There is no tie-break question, forced winner, perfect-balance judgment or middle psychological age. A different group can have a leading side while this group remains tied.
paragraphs.zh: 某组3:3时保留两侧，没有加试题、强制赢家、完美平衡判断或居中的心理年龄。其他组可以有一侧领先，这一组仍然并列。

paragraphs.en: The four groups never combine into a personality type, age profile or maturity grade. Their alternatives can be used together in real life; paired wording has not demonstrated that each pair consists of mutually exclusive psychological traits.
paragraphs.zh: 四组不拼成人格类型、年龄档案或成熟等级。两侧做法在现实中可以配合使用，配对措辞没有证明它们是相互排斥的心理特质。

title.en: Put the choices back into a situation

paragraphs.en: Resources, responsibilities, trust, privacy, health, available time and a task’s risks can affect which approach seems workable. The record does not separate a preference from what was possible. Consider one actual scene and what happened afterward instead of treating a count as a fixed identity.
paragraphs.zh: 资源、责任、信任、隐私、健康、可支配时间和任务风险，都可能影响哪种做法可行。记录无法区分偏好与当时能做到的事；可以回看某个具体情境和后续，不把次数当固定身份。

paragraphs.en: A later different response set does not by itself establish improvement, deterioration or an age change. Optional observation ideas are neither ability tests nor treatment plans. You can keep an approach, combine both sides or choose not to continue an exercise.
paragraphs.zh: 后来回答不同，本身不确立改善、退步或年龄变化。可选观察不是能力考核或治疗方案，可以保留做法、结合两侧，或不再继续练习。

paragraphs.en: This form does not assess age, maturity, intelligence, memory, attention, executive function, cognitive decline or mental health. It cannot compare you with people of the same age or establish emotional competence. A concern about health requires its own appropriate assessment, rather than an inference from these choices.
paragraphs.zh: 表单不评估年龄、成熟度、智力、记忆、注意力、执行功能、认知衰退或心理健康，不能作同龄比较或确立情绪能力。健康担心需要相应的合适评估，不从这些选择推断。

paragraphs.en: Do not use the record for medical or legal judgments, employment or promotion, admissions, security permissions, relationship screening, financial decisions or other consequential decisions. Neither a leading side nor a tie provides evidence for someone’s suitability or future success.
paragraphs.zh: 记录不能用于医疗司法判断、招聘晋升、录取、安全权限、关系筛选、金融或其他高风险决策。领先或并列，都不为某人的适配性或未来成功提供证据。

title.zh: 当前页面内存与公开指南

paragraphs.en: The website uses current-page memory for responses and the current record. It saves no draft or result for another visit and uploads no individual choices. Reloading, changing language, leaving or restoring the page from browser history clears the response state.
paragraphs.zh: 网站仅用当前页面内存存放回答与本次记录，不保存供下次访问恢复的草稿或结果，也不上传逐题选择。刷新、换语、离开或从浏览器历史恢复页面，会清除回答状态。

paragraphs.en: Any copying control provides only the four public guide links, without your counts, selected options or an attempt identifier. The public pages contain general explanations and can be read without answering. You can leave without explaining or sharing a personal record.
paragraphs.zh: 复制功能只提供四个公开指南链接，不带次数、选项或本次作答标识。公开页只有一般解释，无需回答即可阅读。可以直接离开，无需解释或分享私人记录。

title.en: Four full readings, including both sides

paragraphs.en: All four public guides include concrete examples, both approaches, raw-count and tie explanations, context and one optional review. A completed personal record shows the four groups separately and keeps every tied side. No private answer is required to open the general reading.
paragraphs.zh: 四份公开指南都包含具体例子、两种做法、次数与并列解释、情境和一次可选回看。完成后的个人记录分开展示四组，保留所有并列侧；打开一般性读法无需提供私人回答。

paragraphs.en: Coping Rhythm Test describes current everyday choices, without an age model or a maturity grade. There is no paywall or signup needed to finish the questions or read every current guide.
paragraphs.zh: 应对节奏测试描述当前日常选择，没有年龄模型或成熟等级。完成题目与阅读当前所有指南，都无需付费或注册。

question.en: Does this calculate my psychological age?

answer.en: No. It records four separate groups of six relative choices. There is no age conversion, maturity score, actual-age comparison or validated age norm.
answer.zh: 不会。它记录四组各六次相对选择，没有年龄换算、成熟分数、实际年龄比较或经验证的年龄常模。

answer.en: The original form compares two reasonable approaches in the same scene. Choose which is more natural now; it is not a correct-answer test or proof that the alternatives are opposites.
answer.zh: 原题本比较同一场景里的两种合理做法，选择当前更自然的一项。不是正误考试，也不证明两项相反。

answer.en: Each selection adds one to its side. Every six-item group has two counts totaling six, read separately from the other three groups. No overall score is calculated.
answer.zh: 每次选择给所属侧加一次，每组六题两侧合计六，和另外三组分开读，不计算总分。

answer.en: Both sides remain tied in that group. It does not mean perfect balance, intermediate age or a failed test, and you need not change an answer to choose a winner.
answer.zh: 本组保留两侧并列，不表示完美平衡、年龄居中或测试失败，无需改答选赢家。

answer.en: The source has no scored skip choice. All twenty-four valid choices are needed for a personal record; you can leave without a result and read every general guide.
answer.zh: 原题本没有计分跳过选项，个人记录需要二十四次有效选择；可以不产生结果直接离开，阅读所有通用指南。

question.en: Must I answer to read the full guides?
question.zh: 必须先回答才能看全文吗？

answer.en: No. All four public guides are free and include both approaches, examples, count and tie explanations and interpretation limits.
answer.zh: 不用。四份公开指南免费，包含两种做法、例子、次数与并列读法，以及解释边界。

question.en: Are my choices saved or included in shared links?
question.zh: 选择会保存或包含在分享链接里吗？

answer.en: No. This web edition uses current-page memory and clears it on reload, language change or leaving. Copied public guide links contain no choices or counts.
answer.zh: 不会。网站使用当前页面内存，刷新、换语或离开会清除。复制的公开指南链接不带选择或次数。

question.en: Is this a validated coping scale?
question.zh: 这是经验证的应对量表吗？

answer.en: No. These are FermatMind’s original paired questions with a working English translation. The constructs and scoring have not completed psychometric validation and do not inherit evidence from other measures.
